To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a monoclonal anti-huTNFA antibody, that expresses a recurrent idiotope, can be used to precipitate the cytokine.
a mAb78-huCyt complex is formed, that mAb78-hCyt complexes are formed and that mAb78 and mAb78-hUCyt complexes precipitate in agar.
mAb78 binds huTNF alpha with a 1:1 stoichiometry, and that the smallest complexes built up from these reagents are cyclic complexes of 570kD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the interaction between a monoclonal and its corresponding antigen, a cytokine.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the interaction between huTNF alpha, a protein with a complex quaternary structure, and a monoclonally produced mAb.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction between huTNF alpha, a cytokine of great biological importance, and a monoclonally produced antibody.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
huTNF alpha binds to mAb78 in a manner which is different from that by which huTNF alpha interacts with other mAb78 molecules.
the mAb78-humTNF alpha complex formed in the double immunodiffusions assay was not a simple 1:1 mAb78-humorTNF alpha complex, but a complex built up of more mAb78 and huTNF alpha subunits.
mAb78 binds huTNF alpha as a cyclic complex of 3:2 stoichiometry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mAb78-huCytokine interaction is a complex process involving several different modes of interaction.
mAb78 is a neutralizing, but non-precipitating mAb against huTNF alpha.
the interaction between huTNF alpha as a homotrimer and mAb78 as an oligomeric complex is characterized by an extremely tight binding of huTNF subunits to mAb78 subunits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction of huTNF and mAb78 is not a simple 2:2 complex but rather a complex 3:2 complex.
the mode of interaction of huTNFalpha and mAb78 is different from the mode of interaction between huTNFalpha, mAb78, and a second mAb78.
mAb78 is not an antagonist of huTNF, but a ligand for the cytokine.
